newsitem.title: UK: UK airline watchdog eyes charter firms performance.
newsitem.headline: UK airline watchdog eyes charter firms performance.

text.p: The Air Transport Users Council (AUC), the UK consumer watchdog for the airline industry, has published a league table showing which charter airlines are the best and the worst for delays to their flights.

Spanish state airline Iberia's charter service Viva scored best out of the 29 airlines surveyed with the lowest percentage of delays of over one hour in the period between April and October 1996 -- only 4.9 percent of its flights were delayed.
Bottom of the class came Brussels-based independent airline Challenge Air which delayed 65.2 percent of its flights for more than one hour.
British Midland -- with 6 percent of fights delayed -- and British Airways delaying 6.7 percent of flights were ranked second and third best respectively, the survey showed.

While Independent airlines Translift Airways, All Leisure Airlines, Transwede Leisure, Air Atlanta Icelandic, Air Operations Europe and Excalibur Airways were all guilty of delaying 30 percent or more of their flights, it showed.
Excalibur has since folded, said an AUC spokesman, hit by negative publicity about delays and stories of passengers being stranded abroad when their flights were cancelled.

Ian Hamer, chairman of AUC, said "These figures show the huge difference in performance between airlines. Only one flight in twenty is delayed by more than an hour on the best airline. On the worst, two out of every three flights are an hour late and the average delay is almost three hours."
"The public has a right to this information."

AUC said that passengers should check which airline they are flying on before booking a holiday with a charter flight. "If you choose the wrong airline the chances are you will spend a day of your holiday in airport departure lounges," said the watchdog chairman.
